job.title: Contracts Manager
job.description:
Newly created Contracts Manager role created for some to step into a growing, multi-disciplinary construction business, taking ownership of significant projects and helping shape the way they are delivered.

With an established reputation across specialist construction services, the business is expanding its capability to deliver larger projects across New Zealand and the wider Pacific.

To support this growth they are now looking for a commercially astute, delivery-focused Contracts Manager who can take projects from handover through to completion, while helping build the systems, processes and project management capability needed.

The opportunity

As the Contracts Manager, you will take end-to-end responsibility for designated projects, overseeing delivery, commercial performance, programme, risk and client relationships.

You'll have the autonomy to make decisions, lead multidisciplinary project teams and work closely with senior leadership, rather than getting caught up in layers of corporate bureaucracy.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Taking ownership of projects from post-award handover through mobilisation, delivery, practical completion and final commercial close-out.
  • Driving project financial performance, including margins, forecasting, cash flow, variations and claims.
  • Leading project managers, quantity surveyors, site teams, subcontractors and suppliers to deliver safe, high-quality outcomes.
  • Managing construction programmes, procurement, contractual obligations and project risks.
  • Building strong relationships with clients and key stakeholders, resolving issues proactively and protecting commercial outcomes.
  • Developing project controls, processes and delivery capability to support larger, more complex projects in the future.
  • Feeding practical delivery insights back into estimating and tendering to continually improve project performance.
The culture

This is a business with a genuine village feel. It's a more personal, hands-on environment than you might find in a large tier-one contractor, with significantly less hierarchy and more direct access to decision-makers.

You'll be trusted to take ownership, encouraged to contribute ideas and able to see the impact of your work. Rather than being another name in a large corporate structure, you'll be a key part of the business's continued growth.

For someone who enjoys accountability, collaboration and having a real voice in how things operate, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful difference.

We are looking for:

You'll bring strong contractor-side construction experience, with a track record of delivering complex projects and taking ownership of both operational and commercial outcomes.

Ideally, you'll have:
  • Experience across civil, concrete, structures or multidisciplinary construction projects.
  • Strong commercial acumen, including project forecasting, cost control, claims, variations and contract administration.
  • A solid understanding of construction programming, procurement and subcontractor management.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and coordinating operational and commercial stakeholders.
  • A proactive, solutions-focused approach, with the confidence to make decisions and manage risk.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to build lasting relationships with clients, subcontractors and internal teams.
Main contractor delivery experience, along with exposure to regional, remote or Pacific projects, would be advantageous.
  
Why consider this role?
  • A newly created position with the opportunity to shape how projects are delivered.
  • Genuine ownership of project delivery, commercial performance and outcomes.
  • Direct access to senior leadership and less corporate hierarchy.
  • A collaborative, family-oriented culture where people support one another.
  • The chance to help build capability as the business moves into larger and more complex projects.
  • A permanent Auckland-based opportunity offering scope to make a lasting impact.
For more information contact tom@alexanderjames.co.nz

job.title: Contract Finance Analyst
job.description:
This large, fast-paced business plays a key role in keeping us connected, delivering ICT infrastructure, telecommunications, supply chain and logistics services nationwide. They are looking for an experienced Finance Analyst to join their team on an hourly rate contract.

Reporting to the Finance Manager, this is a hands-on role combining financial and management accounting with a strong focus on data analysis and reporting.

We're looking for someone who enjoys getting into the detail, interrogating data, identifying discrepancies and working out practical solutions. You'll work closely with the finance team and data analysts to improve reporting accuracy, streamline processes and ensure operational data flows correctly through to financial reporting and customer billing.

What You'll Be Doing
  • Supporting month-end processes, reconciliations, financial reporting and analysis.
  • Working with Power BI and data analysts to improve reporting, data integrity and visibility.
  • Reviewing 3PL customer billing processes, identifying discrepancies and resolving invoicing issues.
  • Analysing financial and operational data to understand performance, margins and key business drivers.
  • Supporting budgeting, forecasting and financial modelling activities.
  • Identifying opportunities to improve systems, controls and processes, reducing manual work and rework.
  • Working closely with operational and finance stakeholders to investigate issues and implement practical solutions.
What We're Looking For
You'll bring a solid accounting foundation, strong analytical skills and a natural curiosity for understanding how things work.

Ideally, you'll have:
  • A CA/CPA qualification or equivalent experience across financial and management accounting.
  • Strong Power BI exposure, advanced Excel skills and confidence working with complex datasets.
  • Experience in 3PL, logistics or supply chain environments, particularly customer billing and the flow of operational data into invoicing.
  • Strong reconciliation, problem-solving and process improvement skills.
  • The ability to work across finance, operations and data teams to get to the bottom of issues.
  • A proactive, hands-on approach and the confidence to challenge data, question processes and follow things through.
Above all, we're looking for someone who enjoys a role with some traditional month end work combined with solving problems, making sense of complex data and turning findings into improved reporting.

If this sounds like you and you're immediately available for a six-month contract, we'd love to hear from you.

Applicants must have the legal right to work in New Zealand.

job.title: Client Support Specialist
job.description:
We’re looking for an experienced Client Support Specialist to join a leading international law firm based in Auckland.

Working closely with three Partners, you’ll take ownership of their billing, collections and client reporting, while building strong relationships with clients and teams across the firm.

This is more than just a billing role. You’ll become a trusted point of contact for your Partners and their clients, with plenty of autonomy and variety in your day.

What you’ll be doing
  • Managing end-to-end billing, from WIP reports and draft bills through to final invoicing
  • Working closely with Partners and legal teams on billing requirements
  • Managing collections and following up outstanding payments
  • Preparing client, billing and debtor reporting
  • Liaising directly with clients on billing and payment queries
  • Supporting monthly cash collection targets
  • Building strong relationships across the firm
  • Identifying opportunities to improve processes and ways of working
You’ll bring experience in billing, collections or finance administration, ideally within legal or professional services. You’ll be organised, detail-focused and confident working with senior stakeholders, with a strong focus on providing great client service.

This is a great opportunity to join a well-established international firm with a supportive and collaborative culture, while taking ownership of a role where you can really build relationships and make an impact.

Interested? Apply now or get in touch for a confidential chat.

job.title: Accounting & Office Coordinator
job.description:
This organisation is a leading environmental consultancy company with over 20 years' experience. With a reputation for practical solutions and trusted advice, they are a high-performing, growing business looking for an organised and proactive Accounts and Office Coordinator to join their team.

This is a varied, hands-on role at the centre of the business. Reporting to the Director, you will manage day-to-day accounts and administration while supporting payroll, HR, and executive operations. Working closely with leadership and the Consultancy team, you will help ensure the business runs smoothly and efficiently. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys variety, taking ownership, and thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment where your contribution makes a real difference.

You may be returning to work after a career in accounting and be open to incorporating general administration tasks into your day, or an experienced Accounts Assistant/Assistant Accountant looking for even more variety.

Your days will involve, but not limited to:
  • Manage the day to day of accounts including accounts payable, receivable, bank reconciliations, invoicing, and monthly progress claims
  • Process end-to-end payroll, and payroll administration
  • Coordinate HR administration, including onboarding, recruitment support, employee records, training, and Health & Safety documentation
  • Provide executive support to the Director
  • Oversee office administration
You will bring:
  • Proven experience in accounts, including AP, AR, reconciliations, and payroll
  • Excellent initiative, organisation, attention to detail, and communication skills
  • The ability to manage multiple priorities and comfortable working independently
  • Experience supporting a small, privately owned business

This is more than an accounts and administration role. You will work closely with the Director, gain genuine insight into how the business operates, and play an important part in supporting a company that is making a positive impact on New Zealand’s environment.

If you are someone who enjoys being trusted, solving problems, and helping a growing business succeed, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your application today via the link.

job.title: Project Accountant - Process Improvement
job.description:
This global, fast-paced, high volume retail and service business
is looking for an experienced Project Accountant to join its finance team for an 8 month fixed term.

This is a hands-on finance project role sitting outside of BAU, focused on process improvement, balance sheet remediation, systems/workflow improvements and SOP development. You'll be getting under the hood of how things currently work, identifying what's not working and implementing practical improvements.

The role: You'll work closely with finance and operational teams across a range of projects, including:
  • Reviewing finance processes and identifying opportunities to simplify and improve them.
  • Working through balance sheet reconciliation issues and clearing an existing backlog.
  • Investigating high-volume transaction flows across sales, customer payments, finance companies and servicing.
  • Improving month-end processes, controls and GL mappings.
  • Finding practical workarounds within the existing inhouse finance management system.
  • Developing clear and consistent SOPs across the finance function.
About you: We're looking for a senior, hands-on accountant who enjoys getting into the detail, understanding how things work and fixing what isn't working.

You'll ideally bring:
  • Strong financial accounting and balance sheet experience
  • Proven process and systems improvement capability
  • Experience in a high-volume transactional environment - retail or franchise would be ideal
  • Strong Excel skills and confidence working across different systems.
  • An analytical, inquisitive and practical approach
  • The ability to work independently, ask the right questions and get things moving
  • CA/CPA preferred, although strong QBE candidates will be considered
  • Power BI would be a bonus
This will suit someone who can quickly work out what's happening, what's going wrong and how to make it better – and then roll up their sleeves and implement the solution.

Please apply in the first instance so we can have your most recent CV on file. 
We will be responding to applications from Monday 5 October. 
Vacancy managed by Jo Jossevel 

Only candidates with current New Zealand working rights will be considered for this opportunity.
